question: Should Britain match France's arsenal, yes or no?

lines.text: France has test-fired its new M51.3 nuclear-capable missile from a submarine for the first time.
lines.note: France 24: first M51.3 firing from a nuclear-powered submarine, 6 Oct

lines.text: The defence ministry says it carried no warhead.
lines.note: France 24: 'It was not carrying a warhead'

lines.text: It was fired from the submarine Le Vigilant, off the coast of Brittany.
lines.note: France 24 / AeroTime: Le Vigilant, off Brittany (Finistere)

lines.text: It came down in the North Atlantic, hundreds of kilometres from any coastline.

scene.quote: in the North Atlantic, hundreds of kilometres from any coastline

lines.text: President Macron watched from the frigate Auvergne, AeroTime reports.
lines.note: AeroTime: Macron attended from FREMM frigate Auvergne

lines.text: On X, Macron said: today we are stronger, the message has been sent loud and clear.
lines.note: Macron on X, quoted by France 24

scene.quote: Today we are stronger. The message has been sent loud and clear

lines.text: It entered service in October 2025, after a ground test at Biscarrosse in 2023.
lines.note: AeroTime: ground test 18 Nov 2023, Biscarrosse; in service 24 Oct 2025

lines.text: Paris keeps its range secret. Estimates put the M51 family at about 9,000 kilometres.
lines.note: France 24: public estimates around 9,000 km or more

lines.text: France has four ballistic missile submarines.
France 24 says France keeps about 290 nuclear weapons, the world's fourth-largest arsenal.
lines.note: France 24: stockpile of 290 submarine- and air-launched weapons

lines.text: Britain has 225 warheads. Russia and the United States have more than 5,000 each.
lines.note: France 24: Britain 225; Russia and US more than 5,000 each

lines.text: That costs about 5.6 billion euros a year.
lines.note: France 24: roughly 5.6 billion euros a year

lines.text: Macron says France will expand its arsenal. Should Britain match it, yes or no?
lines.note: France 24: Macron said in March France would expand its nuclear arsenal

sources.title: Macron observes test of new nuclear-capable missile without warhead

caption: France M51.3: France has test-fired its new nuclear-capable missile from the submarine Le Vigilant off Brittany for the first time, with no warhead, and President Macron watching. France 24 says France keeps about 290 nuclear weapons, Britain 225. Should Britain match France's arsenal, yes or no?
notes_full: First reported 6 Oct about 08:55 UTC (UNITED24, launch preparations), confirmed 09:50 UTC France 24/AFP, then AeroTime, Insider Paper, Reuters 10:57, UNN; about 3 to 4h old at delivery
Removal-risk: a test that happened, no warhead, official statements only; no target country, no Kaliningrad or Putin threat lines, no toll; neutral yes/no
